table.name: battle
table.purpose: Battles between the Bulgarian Empire and the Latin Empire (Fourth Crusade era, c. 1205-1235), listing commanders, dates, and outcomes. Referenced by ship.lost_in_battle and death.caused_by_ship_id (ships lost in these battles and resulting deaths).

bulgarian_commander.name: bulgarian_commander
bulgarian_commander.description: Name of the Bulgarian commander at the battle (e.g. Tsars Kaloyan, Boril, Ivan Asen II); 'Unknown' when not recorded.

date.name: battle_date
date.description: Date of the battle, stored as free text with inconsistent precision (full day, month+year, or year only).

id.name: battle_id
id.description: Primary key identifying each battle; referenced by ship.lost_in_battle and (indirectly) death.caused_by_ship_id.

latin_commander.name: latin_commander
latin_commander.description: Name of the Latin Empire commander at the battle (e.g. Baldwin I, Henry I, Boniface of Montferrat, John of Brienne); 'Unknown' when not recorded.

name.name: battle_name
name.description: Name of the battle or siege (e.g. Battle of Adrianople, Siege of Constantinople).

result.name: battle_outcome
result.description: Outcome of the battle: 'Bulgarian victory', 'Latin victory', or 'Two Year Truce'.

table.name: death
table.purpose: Casualty records per incident: number of people killed and injured, the ship (or incident) that caused it, and a location note. The note values (Indian districts like Dantewada, Bastar, Bokaro) suggest these rows record casualties of incidents in the Naxal/Maoist conflict in India, despite the ship/battle framing of the rest of the database. Each row is one casualty event.

caused_by_ship_id.name: caused_by_ship_id
caused_by_ship_id.description: Foreign key to ship.id, identifying the ship associated with the casualty event. The column name and the accepted ship lookup (ships with dispositions like Captured, Wrecked, Scuttled, Sank) support this reading. It also joins to battle.id, but that is likely coincidental given the small data size; the ship join is the declared/intended one.

id.name: id
id.description: Primary key of the death table; unique row identifier.

injured.name: injured
injured.description: Count of people injured in the incident. Mostly 0 (11 of 13 rows), with occasional small counts (5, 9).

killed.name: killed
killed.description: Count of people killed in the incident, ranging 0-29.

note.name: note
note.description: Location of the incident as 'place, state' — Indian districts and states (Dantewada/Chhattisgarh, Bastar, Bokaro/Jharkhand, East Champaran/Bihar, Gajapati/Odisha, Kanker/Chhattisgarh). Dantewada, Chhattisgarh appears 5 times.

table.name: ship
table.purpose: Ships (mostly brigs) lost or captured in naval battles, with their type, tonnage, where and how they were lost, and the battle in which they were lost. Referenced by death (deaths caused by a ship) and referencing battle (the battle in which the ship was lost).

disposition_of_ship.name: disposition_of_ship
disposition_of_ship.description: How the ship was lost: Captured, Sank, Scuttled, or Wrecked.

location.name: location
location.description: Sea area where the ship was lost (e.g. English Channel, Mid-Atlantic, SW Approaches).

lost_in_battle.name: lost_in_battle
lost_in_battle.description: Foreign key to battle.id, the battle in which the ship was lost.

name.name: name
name.description: Name of the ship (e.g. HMS Avon, Lettice, Mary).

ship_type.name: ship_type
ship_type.description: Rig/armament class of the ship; all values are brigs, some with gun count (e.g. 18-gun Brig).

tonnage.name: tonnage
tonnage.description: Ship's tonnage as a number (e.g. 225, 391); the value 't' appears where the tonnage is unknown/unrecorded and appears to be a placeholder rather than a real tonnage. Alternative reading: 't' could be a literal token from the source (e.g. an abbreviation), but the placeholder interpretation fits the numeric values better.
